chunks: And from him (Al-Shaykh) from Ibn Abi Umayr from Hammad from Al-Halabi from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

"If he has not yet consummated the marriage with her, but has stipulated a dowry for her, then she is entitled to half of what he stipulated for her, and she inherits, and she observes the waiting period."
As for the dowry, it is obligatory upon him in full if he dies leaving her. The evidence for this is the saying of Allah, the Exalted: 'And give the women [upon marriage] their dower as a free gift.'
And give the women [upon marriage] their dower as a free gift.
So He commanded us to give them the dowry in full, and He did not specify that the wife whose husband dies should receive only half, so it is appropriate that she falls under the general rule.
And this full obligation does not apply to the divorced woman whose husband has not yet consummated the marriage, because we have specified her ruling with a proof and another verse similar to it.
Allah, the Exalted, says: 'And if you divorce them before you have touched them and you have already specified for them an obligation, then [give] half of what you specified...'
So by the explicit meaning of this verse and by many narrations we have previously presented, we have turned away from that apparent [rule of full payment].
And that [specification of half] is not found in the case of the wife whose husband dies and has not yet consummated the marriage with her.
And furthermore, it has been narrated...
ai.seo_question: What is the dowry entitlement for a wife if her husband dies before consummating the marriage?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Tusi elaborates on the distinction between death and divorce by arguing that the general Quranic command to pay the full dowry applies to the deceased husband, as the specific verse for halving the dowry is limited to divorce before consummation. This interpretation reinforces the Shia legal principle that the wife retains her full financial rights and inheritance status even without physical intimacy, provided the marriage contract was valid.
